<description>
Before eae193e750235e4023b3e6313284eede2cd7a022, Connect() only started the connection and returned true. If tor wasn't running the refusal was reported later and only logged under -debug=tor. Since eae193e750 (in v32), every failed reconnect attempt logs:

```
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z connect() to 127.0.0.1:9051 failed after wait: Connection refused (111)
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Error connecting to address 127.0.0.1:9051
2026-11-04T14:14:08Z [warning] tor: Initiating connection to Tor control port 127.0.0.1:9051 failed
```

On a default configured node without tor, this pollutes debug.log with 18 lines every hour.

This move these warnings back to debug.
</description>

[2026-11-06] c:6674882387 comment by fjahr (member):
I agree that the current behavior isn't ideal but it seems that an bigger problem than noisy logs is that you wouldn't see any logs unless you had `-debug=tor` if you had `-torcontrol` set explicitly, i.e. you clearly want to use Tor but there is an issue. That's why I think the current v32 behavior was an improvement to the previous behavior. Instead of reverting, I would suggest a more complete fix that works well for both scenarios: When the user configured Tor they should see logs and when they didn't they should not see them (only with `-debug=tor`).

I have drafted the change so people can decide if they like this more: https://github.com/fjahr/bitcoin/commits/2026-11-torlog/ But note that this also includes a bit of additional improvements like making the logging less noisy when it does happen and deals with losing the connection along the way.
[2026-11-06] c:6684676313 comment by ViniciusCestarii (contributor):
Thanks for reviewing! I agree that logging for tor users is useful. I like @fjahr proposal but also tor is meant to work out of box (without the need of any explicit config), so users that never set tor specific config would not know that tor isn't being used unless they run with `-debug=tor`.

The best both worlds would be what @fjahr proposed + if no explicit tor config, log the first failure once at info level (e.g. "Not using Tor (no control port at 127.0.0.1:9051)") similar to @pinheadmz's `LogWarnThenDebug()` but at info.

@fjahr if you're OK with it, I can pull your commits into this PR (keeping you as author) and add the info-once part on top. Or if you'd rather open your own PR, I'll close this one in favor of it.
